uncited: **Inputs:** A set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$, a set of training views, a target model size budget $B$, and a growth curve function $N(t)$.
**Outputs:** A refined set of Gaussians $\mathcal{G}'$ with size $|\mathcal{G}'| \approx B$.
*   **Gaussian:** Inherits standard 3DGS fields: mean $\mu_k$, covariance $\Sigma_k$, opacity $\alpha_k$, spherical harmonics $\mathbf{c}_k$ [S8, unofficial].
*   **Score Buffer:** A scalar value $S_g$ stored per Gaussian, initialized to zero.
*   **Saliency Map:** A 2D tensor per view representing pixel-wise importance.
**Sample Views:** Select a batch of training views for the current iteration.
**Compute Saliency:** Render the current Gaussians and compute per-pixel saliency.
**Compute Per-Gaussian Score ($S_g$):** For each Gaussian $g_k$, aggregate metrics into a scoring function $F$.
*   Gradient magnitude: Accumulated 2D positional gradients $\tau_k$ [S4, S8, unofficial].
**Select Top Gaussians:** Rank all Gaussians by $S_g$ in descending order.
Typically, one clone and one split (or similar) are performed to double the local density.
**Update Growth Curve:** Increment the iteration counter.
*   **Growth Curve:** A function $N(t)$ mapping iteration $t$ to target count.
*   **Budget Exhaustion:** If the current count exceeds $B$ before the end of training, no further densification occurs.
It is chosen when perceptual quality metrics are more critical than geometric gradient accuracy.
It is applied as a supplement to any densification strategy to refine details after the main structure has converged.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot V)$ per iteration, where $N$ is the number of Gaussians and $V$ is the number of sampled views.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for storing the score buffer and saliency maps.
